launches.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
launches.excerpt: Amazon-owned Zoox and Uber have launched a partnership allowing riders in Las Vegas to hail steering-wheel-free robotaxis directly through the Uber app. This marks the first time Uber has added a purpose-built autonomous vehicle to its network and the first time Zoox has opened its fleet to a third-party application. Customers selecting standard Uber ride options in Las Vegas may be matched with a Zoox vehicle at no additional charge, and users can adjust their app preferences to favour autonomous pods. The robotaxis operate within specific tourist areas, including the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District, while Zoox will also continue to run its standalone application. Additionally, Uber and Zoox have formed a multiyear agreement with MGM Resorts International to become their official rideshare and robotaxi partners in the city. The collaboration involves implementing physical infrastructure changes and custom in-app guidance to streamline pickups and drop-offs at complex casino locations. Following the Las Vegas launch, the companies plan to expand to Los Angeles, with a full Uber integration scheduled for 2027 following an initial standalone launch. This initiative forms part of Uber’s broader strategy to act as a platform for various autonomous vehicle operators after abandoning its own self-driving technology development. Meanwhile, Uber's partnership network has experienced some friction, as Waymo recently announced plans to end its exclusive arrangement with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028.

launches.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
launches.excerpt: Apple is launching a new research study app developed in partnership with healthcare-focused artificial intelligence company OpenEvidence to examine how people utilise clinically grounded AI for health-related queries. The tech giant aims to recruit up to 200,000 participants in the United States who are aged 21 or older, use an iPhone 15 or later, and run iOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled. The study is scheduled to run for more than twelve months, allowing users to ask everyday medical questions and receive simplified answers derived from clinical data sources such as the Journal of the American Medical Association, The New England Journal of Medicine, and Nature. Participants will be asked to rate the app responses, provide feedback, and complete monthly surveys. Users can additionally choose to share personal metrics from HealthKit, including sleep, activity, resting heart rate, and lab results, to receive more personalised suggestions and better prepare for medical appointments. Apple stated that all collected data will be anonymised prior to transmission to a secure third-party cloud provider, will not be utilised for training artificial intelligence models, and will have query and response data deleted by OpenEvidence after twenty-four hours. The application became available for download in the United States.

launches.title: Grok 4.7 now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
launches.excerpt: The Grok 4.7 model has been released in the Kiro integrated development environment and command-line interface for the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Developed by SpaceXSI, the software is designed as the organisation's most capable model for knowledge work and coding tasks. It features the ability to maintain focus on complex tasks lasting several hours and incorporates self-correction mechanisms to verify outputs before proceeding. Compared to the previous version, Grok 4.6, the new release offers improved planning and error recovery capabilities during repository-scale coding operations. The model is currently provided with experimental support and includes a 500K context window. Pricing is structured by token volume, with requests up to 200K tokens incurring a 2.7x credit multiplier, while requests exceeding 200K tokens are billed at 5.4x. Kiro administrators retain control over model availability, allowing organisations to restrict or permit access according to their internal policies. To utilise the new model, users must update their IDE or CLI to the latest version and restart the application to select it from the menu. launches.title: C++26 stumbles at finish line over Contracts dispute
launches.excerpt: The upcoming C++26 programming language release faces a potential delay due to a major dispute among technical maintainers over a security-enhancing feature known as Contracts. Contracts permit developers to include preconditions, postconditions, and assertions in code to catch errors that could otherwise result in undefined behaviour. The disagreement culminated in October when the Draft International Standard of C++26 failed its ISO ballot after receiving 13 votes in favour, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, falling short of the requirement that negative votes must not exceed 25 percent. The feature has been discussed for a decade, having previously been removed from C++20 over concerns regarding dangerous defaults. C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup and his colleagues opposed the current C++26 proposal, arguing in a paper that it threatens the language by adding complexity, bloat, and messy implementation. Conversely, committee member Andreas Fertig criticised the late veto as damaging to the collaborative process and accused detractors of refusing to accept a compromise. However, C++ Alliance CEO Harry Bott viewed the failed draft as the standardisation process functioning as intended. The failure risks pushing the expected release date of the language into next year, potentially requiring the informal name C++27. The ISO working group is scheduled to meet in Brazil to consider options, which include removing Contracts from the specification, moving the feature to a separate technical specification, or performing a minor revision for another vote.

launches.title: OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they’re doomed if they don’t use them
launches.excerpt: OpenAI has unveiled two new security products under its Daybreak platform, warning that business security now depends on utilising frontier models for defence. Speaking at a keynote address, OpenAI President Greg Brockman stated that organisations must reorient their security practices around the capabilities of these models. The newly launched Daybreak Red Team product uses OpenAI models to test web applications for vulnerabilities through automated continuous scanning and helps teams validate reported flaws and patches. geo.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
geo.excerpt: French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021. The seventy-seven-year-old actor withdrew his appeal on the exact day it was scheduled to go to trial.

geo.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
geo.excerpt: Saudi Arabia has dismissed the commander of the coalition fighting in Yemen as Iran-backed Houthi rebels advance towards the temporary capital of Aden. According to a royal decree cited by the official Saudi Press Agency, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad bin Abdulaziz al-Salman was removed from his post and appointed as an advisor for military affairs to the Minister of Defence. Chief of staff General Fayyad bin Hamed bin Ruqad al-Ruwaili has been named as the coalition's new commander. The military shake-up coincides with Houthi forces seizing territory on Yemen's southern coast following a strategic withdrawal by Saudi-backed government forces. Military sources reported that Houthi fighters have advanced to Khor Omairh, located about 100 kilometres west of Aden, and reached positions close to government lines at Qawah. The internationally recognised government announced it was pulling back from areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to concentrate on defending Aden and the province of Lahj. Residents in Aden have reported an increased security presence with additional checkpoints and identity checks, alongside growing anxiety over the advancing rebels. The renewed conflict follows a dormant period in the civil war since 2022, with the recent fighting reignited as a spillover of wider regional tensions. Government sources stated that forces are currently redeploying and reorganising along front lines to prepare for a counter-offensive to recapture lost territory.

invest.title: Anthropic’s IPO lands as the embattled AI trade looks for a much-needed bright spot
invest.excerpt: Anthropic is scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday in what is considered one of the most important technology initial public offerings in recent years. Major tech companies including Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are collectively investing $26 billion at the expected IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share. Early backer Amazon also holds a substantial stake in the artificial intelligence lab. The offering could yield over $90 billion in proceeds, helping the company fund the massive technology and infrastructure required to build and host its frontier models. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $104 billion through the first nine months of 2026 and carries staggering spending commitments exceeding $900 billion. These obligations include a ten-year, $110 billion agreement with Amazon and $125 billion to $150 billion intended for AI chips from Google. Cloud partners Amazon, Google, and Microsoft account for 31% of these contractual obligations. The IPO arrives during a challenging period for the technology sector, which faces rising interest rates, recent Democratic midterm election victories, and the sudden ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Google will own approximately 13% of Anthropic following the public offering and is backstopping the lab's lease commitments to Terawulf. Financial institutions including Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley have also offered $63 billion for Broadcom AI chips that Anthropic will rent.
